findings.title: Elysium's node is built with an end-of-life Go release that lacks two amd64 compiler fixes, and no EVM result was found to depend on them
findings.difference: The Elysium endpoint reports nitro/vlocal+unknown-unknown/linux-amd64/go1.25.12. Go 1.25 left support when go1.27.0 shipped on 2026-08-19. go1.25.13 fixed, among others, issue 79874, where the prove pass emits a 32 bit slice mask for a 64 bit slice operation on targets that sign-extend 32 bit constants (amd64 named), so a slice with a start index of 2^32 or more advances too little, and issue 80517, where prove applies a fact before the point where it holds and drops a bounds check, shown on amd64 as a call through an out-of-range function table entry. Arbitrum One and Robinhood Chain run go1.27.3, which is inside the range of the separate F-117 fault.
findings.mechanism: Both faults change behaviour only on unusual shapes. Issue 79874 needs a slice start of 2^32 or more that the compiler has proved in bounds. The interpreter never slices calldata, code, memory or return data with such an index: a copy or load with a larger offset is clamped to the data length or charged for memory expansion first, and a zero-length copy or hash at a large offset touches no slice. The new offsets.py vectors aim at exactly that region (offsets from 2^31 to 2^256-1 for CALLDATALOAD, CALLDATACOPY, CODECOPY, KECCAK256, MCOPY and RETURNDATACOPY) and Elysium returns the specified word or failure on every one. Issue 80517 removes a bounds check whose failure would otherwise panic; on a correct program the check never fires, so it can only turn an existing out-of-range bug of the node into a silent read. The PoolManager paths that depend on these copies are the hook result copy (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:148), the revert bubbling copy (src/libraries/CustomRevert.sol:109), and the arithmetic in src/libraries/FullMath.sol:21-54; all match on the battery, the targeted set, the script sets and 3,515 mined swaps. The settled state is computed by the consensus-v61 WebAssembly machine built with go1.25.9 (F-119), which predates both fixes as well but runs on a different target.
findings.impact: None found. A miscompile in the node would make the Elysium operator's node disagree with an honest validator, which with one whitelisted validator (cycle 11) is the operator agreeing with itself.
findings.preconditions: The Elysium operator keeps building from go1.25.12, and some function on the interpreter or state path has one of the two shapes. Neither shape was found; the Go source of the node build is not public, so the check is by its answers.
findings.mitigations: The deployer can ask Kinetiq to rebuild the node with a supported Go release and to publish the version and commit of the build. LPs need do nothing.

cleared.check: Opcode battery, targeted set, call semantics, the deployed-bytecode script sets 1 and 2, and mined swaps with replay, rerun on 2026-11-25 for this unit's chain ids with client versions logged before each step.
cleared.result: Every vector and call semantics word is as specified, sets 1 and 2 are identical to Ethereum apart from Elysium script 189 (gas), and 15,315 mined swaps pass the tick relation with every pair explained. The math in src/libraries/FullMath.sol:14-54, SqrtPriceMath.sol, TickMath.sol, TickBitmap.sol and BitMath.sol:16-48 therefore gets the specified opcode results on these nodes.

cleared.check: Copy, load and hash opcodes with operand offsets from 2^31 to 2^256-1 (offsets.py, 200 vectors per chain), aimed at Go slice and index arithmetic near 2^32 and 2^64, which the PoolManager meets in the hook result copy and revert bubbling (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:148, src/libraries/CustomRevert.sol:109) and in calldata decoding.
cleared.result: No mismatch on 600 vectors: loads and copies past the end return zeros at every offset up to 2^256-1, zero-length hashes, copies and memory copies at those offsets succeed without touching memory, and return data copies fail exactly when offset plus length exceeds the 40 bytes returned, including when the sum overflows. The arm64 build of Arbitrum One, both builds behind Robinhood Chain and the amd64 go1.25.12 build of Elysium agree.

cleared.check: The interpreter files of fork 0e44603 (core/vm instructions.go, eips.go, evm.go, jump_table.go, analysis_legacy.go, common.go) against upstream go-ethereum v1.17.4: does any change alter an arithmetic, comparison, shift, jump, copy, hash or call result that src/ uses?
cleared.result: No. analysis_legacy.go is identical. instructions.go changes GASPRICE, BLOCKHASH and NUMBER (L1 values), SELFDESTRUCT (burn and Stylus guard) and adds address filter touches and multi-gas bookkeeping around CALL, CALLCODE, DELEGATECALL and STATICCALL; eips.go makes BLOBBASEFEE fail; evm.go routes precompiles through an advanced call with the caller's value and keeps pre-Amsterdam system call transfers; common.go reads code size limits from chain parameters. The PoolManager bytecode uses none of GASPRICE, BLOCKHASH, NUMBER, BLOBBASEFEE or SELFDESTRUCT, and the call changes do not touch return data, value transfer or success.

cleared.check: Lead L-749: does the consensus-v61 replay module that validators JIT compile with Cranelift contain a function with more than 2^24 SSA values or a br_table near the aarch64 reach limit of the October 2026 advisories?
cleared.result: No. replay.wasm of the consensus-v61 release (sha256 9d6d28c4...60af, 27,178,379 bytes) has 14,494 defined functions and 7,434,371 instructions. The largest function has 29,997 instructions, 14 locals and 1,156 blocks, so its SSA values are bounded far below 16.7 million; the product of locals and blocks never exceeds 16,184. The largest br_table has 1,485 targets against a limit of about 262,144, and no function has a table above 4,096 targets.

cleared.check: P1 to P3 against every precompile and system address of the three nodes: what do 336 addresses (0x01 to 0x11f, 0x800 to 0x81f, 0xa4b000 to 0xa4b00f, 0xfffe, 0xffff) answer to empty calldata, balanceOf(PoolManager) and transfer(to, 1) when the PoolManager is the caller?
cleared.result: No address answers balanceOf with a value that tracks a balance or accepts transfer with a 32 byte true. The ArbOS precompiles revert on all three shapes (0x70 with an access control error, 0xff with debug precompiles disabled), so a take, sync or settle naming them reverts. The Ethereum precompiles answer as on Ethereum, and the identity precompile echoes the calldata, which makes transfer fail the check at src/types/Currency.sol:68 and makes sync record a constant that settle subtracts from itself (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-365). Elysium has no extra address.

cleared.check: Native token mint and burn through ArbNativeTokenManager (0x73), which would change the native balance that settle never reads but that take pays out of (src/types/Currency.sol:44-52).
cleared.result: Off on all three chains: getNativeTokenManagementFrom() returns 0. Turning it on is a chain owner action.

cleared.check: A1 on the public Nitro master: do the endTxNow transaction types run contract code before StateDB.Prepare resets transient storage, so that a stale unlock flag or synced currency (src/libraries/Lock.sol:13-25, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:17-36) could be read?
cleared.result: No. Deposits mint and transfer without invoking the EVM, internal transactions run ArbOS updates from the ArbOS address, and retryable submissions move balances and emit precompile logs; each returns before Prepare and runs no contract code. Retry transactions return endTxNow false and pass through Prepare before the EVM runs. This repeats the reading at the pinned commit on the newest public source.

cleared.check: Upcoming forks for the next six months: which ArbOS or parameter changes are scheduled or proposed, and what do they change for the PoolManager?
cleared.result: No ArbOS upgrade is scheduled on any of the three chains (getScheduledUpgrade() is zero), no proposal for an ArbOS after 61 exists on the Arbitrum forum, and Robinhood Chain's notices list node releases only. The one approved change is the Arbitrum One and Nova L1 pricing update (parentGasFloorPerToken 10 to 16, perBatchGasCharge 210,000 to 480,000), which waits for Ethereum's Glamsterdam and changes only the L1 fee a transaction pays. If an ArbOS 70 later turns on the Amsterdam set, its new opcodes (SLOTNUM, DUPN, SWAPN, EXCHANGE) do not occur in the bytecode, and the new state charge for a value call to an empty account (fork evm.go line 312) can only make a native take fail as a whole with NativeTransferFailed (src/types/Currency.sol:48-53), which reverts the caller's debit with it.

leads.question: Which Go toolchain and Nitro commit build Elysium's sequencer and its one whitelisted validator, and does any function of core/vm, core/state or holiman/uint256 compiled with go1.25.12 for amd64 have the shape of Go issues 79874 or 80517 (check with the prove debug output of a go1.25.12 build)?
leads.why: The public endpoint reports an unversioned build on an end-of-life toolchain. The endpoint's answers match on every vector, but the producer may run another build.

leads.question: When getScheduledUpgrade() on Elysium turns nonzero, rerun precscan.py and the P1 to P5 call shapes against the new precompile and the ElysiumCoreWriter predeploy before the activation time, and read whether the keeper delivers callbacks as ordinary transactions.
leads.why: This is the only scheduled change in the family that can add a system address, and the scan is ready to rerun.

leadResults.answer: Not answerable on 2026-11-25. arbOSVersion() returns 116 (ArbOS 61) and getScheduledUpgrade() returns zeros on Elysium, so no new code sits at any address yet. A scan of 336 addresses from the PoolManager address with empty calldata, balanceOf(PoolManager) and transfer shows only the stock precompiles, all reverting or answering as on Ethereum (raw/precscan.json). The documentation pages for the keeper lane and the read precompile are unchanged since 2026-11-02 and 2026-09-21 and still name no address or selector. precscan.py in the work directory is ready to rerun when an upgrade is scheduled.
Same state as L-770 on 2026-11-25: ArbOS 61, nothing scheduled, stock precompile set, documentation unchanged and without addresses or funding functions.

The keeper lane page (updated 2026-11-02) still says only that outcomes are delivered back to the originating contract with gas refunded from a HYPE escrow on the predeploy. The public Nitro master has no transaction type that runs contract code outside StateDB.Prepare, so a callback can only keep its own transient map if Kinetiq's fork adds one; that fork is not public and the upgrade is not scheduled.

replay.wasm of the consensus-v61 release was parsed: 14,494 functions, the largest 29,997 instructions with 14 locals and 1,156 blocks, the largest br_table 1,485 targets. Neither the 2^24 SSA value limit nor the aarch64 br_table reach limit of about 262,144 entries is within reach. The file was taken from the release whose page states module root 0xc10cd7ec...dc97; the root was not recomputed here.
Issuer level (a token signer). Not worked this cycle, whose scope excludes token sweeps.
Operator level. Filtering still starts at 2026-06-24 10:00 UTC (getTransactionFilteringFrom() = 0x6a3baaa0); the rule files stay off chain.

The running build v3.13.0-rc.9+b72783f is still private: go.mod at v3.13.0, rc.9, rc.10 and v3.12.5 returns 404 and proxy.golang.org does not know b72783f. The public master's StartTxHook and precompile registry were read and match the v3.12.4 behaviour (no contract code before Prepare, no precompile after 0x74), and the node's answers at 336 addresses agree with that registry.
Pool-creator level hook ownership. Not worked this cycle, whose scope excludes hook sweeps.
